title: He had everything.
paragraphs:
He had everything.
And God called him a fool.

Not poor.
Not struggling.
Not desperate.

You can win in life…
and still lose your soul.

You can build, expand, succeed—
and still stand bankrupt before eternity.
And here’s the part no one tells you:
You might be closer to that man than you think.
Because the rich fool didn’t look evil.

The kind of man people admire.
The kind of life people chase.

He had barns full of grain—
but a heart empty of God.

He had plans for years—
but no awareness of eternity.
He spoke to his soul like he was in control.
That’s the open wound in this story.
Let me say it plainly, kapatid:
You can look blessed… and still be spiritually dead.

You can be surrounded by abundance
and still be starving where it matters most.
And this is where it gets uncomfortable.
Because this isn’t just about a man in a story.
We build our modern barns differently.

Savings accounts.
Businesses.
Careers.
Followers.
Achievements.
Reputation.
And deep inside, we whisper the same lie:
But security built without God is just a decorated illusion.
Because the real issue wasn’t what he had.
The rich fool never once acknowledged God.

Not in his increase.
Not in his planning.
Not in his future.
That’s pride wearing success as a disguise.

Assumes control.
Assumes tomorrow.
Assumes ownership over what was never ours to begin with.
“But God said to him, ‘Fool! This night your soul is required of you, and the things you have prepared, whose will they be?’”
“This night your soul is required of you.”
Some scholars interpret this as a divine interruption—a reminder that life is not owned, only entrusted.
You don’t control your final breath.
And suddenly, the barns didn’t matter.
Because none of it could stand in front of God.
What are you building that cannot follow you into eternity?

Your bank account will remain.
Your house will remain.
Your business will remain.
And in that moment, there will be no titles.
Because this is where many people miss it.
The rich fool wasn’t condemned for being wealthy.
He was condemned for being empty toward God.
“So is the one who lays up treasure for himself and is not rich toward God.”
You can have everything in this world…
And still have nothing where it matters most.
And here’s the truth that hits hard:
We are all born spiritually bankrupt.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.”

Every one of us has lived moments—
or entire seasons—
Where we trusted in what we could build, control, and secure.
“For the wages of sin is death…”
So now we stand in the same danger as the rich fool.
But because of distance from God.
Because Jesus didn’t just tell this story to warn.

Building lives without God.
Trusting in temporary things.
Living like eternity was optional.
“For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though He was rich, yet for your sake He became poor, so that you by His poverty might become rich.”

He lived the life we couldn’t live—
perfect, holy, fully surrendered to the Father.

Then He took our sin—
our pride, our self-reliance, our spiritual blindness—
and carried it to the cross.
“He Himself bore our sins in His body on the tree, that we might die to sin and live to righteousness.”
Not because He was a fool.
“He was buried, and He was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures.”
Your story doesn’t have to end like the rich fool.
You don’t have to stand before God empty.
You don’t have to cling to things that cannot save.
You can become rich toward God.
But by repenting and trusting in Jesus Christ.

Turning from self-trust.
Turning from pride.
Turning from building your life without God.

Placing your full trust in Jesus—
His life, His death, His resurrection—
“For by grace you have been saved through faith. And this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God, not a result of works, so that no one may boast.”
This is where grace explodes into the story.
So now the question becomes personal.
What are you trusting in right now?

Is it your money?
Your plans?
Your stability?
Your success?
Because only one of those can stand in eternity.
If you feel that tension in your chest…
That sense that something isn’t right—

“Lord, I’ve been building my life without You.
I’ve trusted in things that cannot save.
Forgive me.
Change me.
I surrender to You.
Jesus, You are my only hope.”
And if you’re already walking with Christ…
Because following Jesus isn’t about having Him as an addition.
If this spoke to you—don’t ignore it.
